title: Tata Motors Ltd - 544569 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Tata Motors Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 23% to ₹19,300 crore on 26% volume growth; EBITDA margin fell 60 bps to 11.7% on commodity costs.
summary.overview: Standalone wholesales reached about 108,700 units, up 26% YoY, with growth in every product line. Revenue grew 23% to ₹19,300 crore and EBITDA was ₹2,300 crore at an 11.7% margin, down 60 bps, as steel, aluminium and copper inflation was largely offset by price increases and operating leverage. Free cash flow swung to ₹1,100 crore positive from negative ₹1,800 crore, helped by a ₹3,474 crore working-capital outflow last year that did not recur and by a one-off Indonesia advance. Management guided to a double-digit Q2 domestic growth and a further 2.5% price increase from July 1, while flagging continued commodity pressure.

segments.name: Intermediate and light CV (ILMCV)
segments.commentary: 17.1K units, up 16% YoY; VAHAN share dipped slightly on Western Zone supply-chain constraints.

segments.name: SCV Pickup
segments.commentary: 38.3K units, up 35% YoY; EV penetration reached double digits in May and June, with over 3,200 SCV EV retails in Q1 (about 4x YoY).

segments.name: CV Passenger (buses and vans)
segments.commentary: 18.7K units, up 23% YoY; VAHAN share up about 490 bps; around 4,500 government orders on hand and over 850 e-bus orders.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: 8.1K units, up 35% YoY; about 2,000 Indonesia vehicles shipped in Q1 against a 70,000-unit order to be supplied over FY27 and FY28.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 domestic CV volumes expected to show healthy double-digit YoY growth, based on July trends.
Further commodity inflation (steel, rubber) expected; net price increase of 2.5% taken from July 1, 2026, with cost management as first line of defence.
Indonesia 70,000-unit order to be supplied over FY27 and FY28; ramp-up under way.
Iveco transaction: final regulatory approval (one pending) expected by end August 2026; tender offer expected early September 2026, closing early November 2026.
Investment spend guided at 2% to 4% of revenue; Q1 was ₹515 crore (about 2.7%).
Management expects operating leverage to continue as other expenses grow slower than revenue.
capex_capacity: Standalone capex ₹554 crore in Q1, in line with the investment plan.
Intra EV constrained by imported cell supply, not in-house assembly capacity; management expects cell supply debottlenecked by end of Q1 FY27 after orders placed about two months earlier.
Supply constraints in sheet metal, castings and forgings across the industry; debottlenecking actions taken with more in pipeline, throughput improved toward end of Q1 and into Q2.
Lucknow plant crossed 10 lakh cumulative commercial vehicles produced.
FleetEdge installed base above 1 million vehicles.
demand_pricing: Industry wholesales grew about 18% YoY in Q1; Company volumes grew about 26%. E-way bills up 12.4%, diesel consumption and FASTag collections also rising.
Fleet utilisation improved month on month in Q1 but stayed slightly below Q1 FY26, attributed to high H2 FY26 sales volumes.
Price increases taken during the quarter were largely passed through and added about 140 bps to EBIT margin via realisation (₹402 crore).
Commodity headwind of ₹649 crore (340 bps) on variable costs; volume and mix added ₹686 crore.
Tamil Nadu demand recovering month on month and close to normal in June.
Tipper utilisation seasonally lower during monsoon, expected to pick up mid-September.

qa_highlights.question: Will domestic CV growth be double digit for full year, and how do Indonesia dispatches split across FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early for full-year view; Q2 expected to show double-digit growth. Indonesia 70,000 units to be supplied over FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV demand outlook, Intra EV response and capacity, and will the Q2 price hike cover cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: EV demand seen as positive, with over 850 e-bus orders and further PM e-Bus Sewa tenders expected. Capacity is not the constraint; imported cell lead times are. Further commodity pressure expected; 2.5% net price hike from July 1.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a limit to price hikes given steel and rubber surges, and how is discounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost containment is the first lever; price increases are needed beyond that. The MY26 range helped stabilise prices. Cumulative price increase this year described as significant; no discounting figures given.

qa_highlights.question: Is working capital and FCF strength structural or one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly carry-over from Q4 and working-capital discipline plus operating profit. The Indonesia advance was a one-off that helped Q1 cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: E-truck profitability versus ICE and PLI status?
qa_highlights.answer: Profitability currently lower than ICE trucks because of low scale; will improve with scale and localisation. Some EV trucks delivered before PLI certificates due to regulatory delays, to meet customer commitments.

qa_highlights.question: How are operators' profitability and freight rates faring after diesel price rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has no index; anecdotally, diesel increases are being passed through and operator profitability should recover gradually.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (steel, aluminium, copper, rubber) and further cost pressure in Q2 against a 2.5% July price hike.
Supply constraints in castings, forgings and sheet metal, and imported EV cell lead times, which could cap volumes.
Cash tax now recurring (₹500 crore in Q1 vs ₹20 crore a year earlier); Q1 working-capital benefit partly one-off from Indonesia advance.
Regulatory delay in PLI certificates for EV trucks, with some vehicles delivered before PLI approval.
Iveco transaction approval timing (one approval pending) and tender offer schedule.
Fleet utilisation still below prior-year Q1 levels; tipper utilisation seasonality.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, EV demand and cash flow, with clear caution on commodity costs and supply chain. Management was evasive on the pricing limit and on e-truck profitability, and gave no full-year volume view.
key_quotes: Q1 was a quarter of execution on the commitments we made at the start of the year.
So, despite the margin moderation, absolute profit growth has kept pace with revenue.
In summary, operating leverage and improved realisation have absorbed almost all of the significant commodity headwind.

adds.what: Standalone capex of ₹554 crore in Q1 in line with investment plan; no specific new plant, line or capacity addition with timing disclosed

growth.why: Management guided to healthy double-digit YoY domestic CV volume growth in Q2 FY27 based on July trends, backed by a 70,000-unit Indonesia order over FY27-FY28 (about 2,000 shipped in Q1) and a 2.5% price increase from July 1, though no new capacity with timing was quantified and parts constraints were flagged.
